question.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form ${P}_{n}(y)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6{y}^{3}+50{y}^{2}+100y & =5{y}^{2}+25y \\ 6{y}^{3}+45{y}^{2}+100y & =25y \\ 6{y}^{3}+45{y}^{2}+75y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $3y.$ We can factor out the $3y$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{y}^{3}+45{y}^{2}+75y & =0 \\ 3y(2{y}^{2}+15y+25) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $2{y}^{2}+15y+25$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3y(2{y}^{2}+15y+25) & =0 \\ 3y(2y+5)(y+5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $y=0,$ $y=-\frac{5}{2},$ and $y=-5.$
